tagline: Home of the giant Phra Pathom Chedi, next door to Bangkok, with old markets, floating markets, and loads of famous food
introHtml:
Nakhon Pathom sits just west of Bangkok — a short drive out via Phetkasem or the Pinklao–Nakhon Chai Si road and you're there. The first thing most people picture is Phra Pathom Chedi, the huge stupa standing right in the middle of town. The markets and food streets around it stay busy all day. It's an old town that's been woven into everyday life for a long time.

Head out of town toward Sam Phran and Nakhon Chai Si and you hit fruit orchards, the banks of the Tha Chin River, floating markets, and several old riverside markets. Bangkok folks often come for the day to make merit, walk the markets, grab khao moo daeng or moo satay, then take home khao lam and fruit.
bestTime: November–February, cool and dry with little rain — easy to walk the markets and explore the riverside all day

highlights.name: Phra Pathom Chedi
highlights.blurb: The huge stupa in the middle of town that's the symbol of the province. People come to make merit, walk the grounds around it, and browse the markets nearby that stay busy all day.

highlights.name: Markets around the chedi and the night market
highlights.blurb: The food quarter circling Phra Pathom Chedi, with khao moo daeng, moo satay, noodles, and snacks to graze on. In the evening a night market opens up.

highlights.name: Sam Phran riverside and fruit orchards
highlights.blurb: The Sam Phran area along the Tha Chin River has Sampran Riverside, fruit orchards, and riverside restaurants — an easy spot near Bangkok to relax and eat.

highlights.name: Don Wai Floating Market and Nakhon Chai Si riverside markets
highlights.blurb: Old markets along the Tha Chin River in the Sam Phran–Nakhon Chai Si area, with local food, riverside dining, and boat rides past the orchards.

highlights.name: Phutthamonthon
highlights.blurb: A large Buddhist park right by the Bangkok border, with the standing Phra Sri Sakyamuni Buddha in the middle of a wide lawn. Shady trees, and people come to walk and cycle.

highlights.name: Khao lam and Nakhon Chai Si pomelo
highlights.blurb: The province's signature pair: fragrant grilled khao lam and pomelo from the orchards around Nakhon Chai Si. You can buy them to take home all along the way.

foodScene.name: Khao moo daeng and crispy pork
foodScene.note: A local favorite around Phra Pathom Chedi, with several long-running shops. Thick red sauce poured over red pork and crispy pork.

foodScene.name: Moo satay
foodScene.note: The chedi area has charcoal-grilled moo satay with peanut dipping sauce and pickled cucumber relish — a town staple people stop for.

foodScene.name: Nakhon Pathom khao lam
foodScene.note: Sticky rice grilled in bamboo tubes, with both custard and black bean fillings. Lined up for sale around the chedi and along the road — the province's standard souvenir.

foodScene.name: Nakhon Chai Si pomelo and fruit
foodScene.note: Orchards around Nakhon Chai Si and Sam Phran grow well-known pomelo, with seasonal fruit sold roadside — easy to grab on the way home.

foodScene.name: Tha Chin riverside food
foodScene.note: Restaurants along the Tha Chin River around Sam Phran–Nakhon Chai Si serve freshwater fish, prawns, and made-to-order dishes in a riverside setting.

foodScene.name: Noodles and market food
foodScene.note: The markets around the chedi and the old riverside markets have noodles, rice-and-curry, and snacks to graze on all day.

foodScene.name: Thai sweets and floating-market treats
foodScene.note: Don Wai Floating Market and the old markets have fresh Thai sweets — thong yip, khanom krok, and local desserts to take home.

foodScene.name: Cafes and chill spots around the university
foodScene.note: The Salaya area near Mahidol and several streets have plenty of new cafes and work-friendly spots to drop into.

attractions.name: Phra Pathom Chedi
attractions.blurb: The huge stupa in the middle of town that's the symbol of the province. People come to make merit, walk the grounds, and browse the markets nearby.

attractions.name: Sanam Chandra Palace
attractions.blurb: An old palace from the reign of King Rama VI, near the chedi, with several residences set in a shady garden. Good for admiring the architecture and taking photos.

attractions.name: Phutthamonthon
attractions.blurb: A large Buddhist park with the standing Phra Sri Sakyamuni Buddha in the middle of a wide lawn. Shady trees, good for walking and cycling.

attractions.name: Don Wai Floating Market
attractions.blurb: An old market along the Tha Chin River in the Sam Phran area, with local food, riverside dining, and boat rides past the orchards on both banks.

attractions.name: Sampran Riverside
attractions.blurb: A riverside park on the Tha Chin with big trees, fruit orchards, a green market, and activities centered on organic farming.

attractions.name: Wat Rai Khing
attractions.blurb: A well-known temple along the Tha Chin River in the Sam Phran area, with Luang Pho Wat Rai Khing to pay respects to and a riverside market out front to eat at.

attractions.name: Pathom Asoke Park and Nakhon Chai Si farm country
attractions.blurb: The Nakhon Chai Si area has fruit orchards, pomelo groves, and riverside farmland — drive along the orchards and buy fresh fruit.

attractions.name: Thai Human Imagery Museum
attractions.blurb: A wax museum in the Nakhon Chai Si area, displaying lifelike figures of notable people and Thai ways of life. A walk-through the whole family can enjoy.
